text.en: Lady Nairne kept her authorship secret, even writing as "Mrs. Bogan, of Bogan". Only after she died did her sister agree, on January 16, 1846, to "letting it be known that she wrote them".
text.es: Lady Nairne mantuvo en secreto que era la autora, e incluso firmaba como "Mrs. Bogan, of Bogan". Solo después de su muerte aceptó su hermana, el 16 de enero de 1846, "letting it be known that she wrote them" (que se supiera que ella las había escrito).

source.en: Charles Rogers, Life and Songs of the Baroness Nairne (1869), memoir pp. xxxvi to xxxvii and lxxvii to lxxviii, read from the scan
source.es: Charles Rogers, Life and Songs of the Baroness Nairne (1869), memoria, pp. xxxvi a xxxvii y lxxvii a lxxviii, leído en el escaneo

text.en: At Gask, where Lady Nairne grew up, a small table reads "Charles, Prince of Wales, breakfasted at this table in the low Drawing Room at Gask, September 11th, 1745." Around 1900 his bonnet, brogues, spurs and a lock of his hair could still be seen there.
text.es: En Gask, donde se crió Lady Nairne, una mesita lleva la inscripción "Charles, Prince of Wales, breakfasted at this table in the low Drawing Room at Gask, September 11th, 1745." (Carlos, príncipe de Gales, desayunó en esta mesa en el salón bajo de Gask, el 11 de septiembre de 1745). Hacia 1900 aún podían verse allí su boina, sus zapatos, sus espuelas y un mechón de su pelo.

source.en: George Henderson, Lady Nairne and Her Songs (about 1900), pp. 19 to 22, read from the scan
source.es: George Henderson, Lady Nairne and Her Songs (hacia 1900), pp. 19 a 22, leído en el escaneo
